stories.name: Marc Dantzker
stories.story_summary: Marine biologist Marc Dantzker and the FishEye Collaborative built the UPAC-360 (Underwater Passive Acoustic Camera), a novel instrument combining a 7-hydrophone spatial audio array with an Insta360 X3 camera in an underwater housing to study coral reef soundscapes. Fieldwork was conducted on coral reefs in Curaçao, with data collected through December 2025. In a single 15-minute recording session the system enabled identification of 46 reef fish species by sound.
stories.why_it_matters: First-of-its-kind tool combining spatial audio and 360° video to identify reef fish species by sound — a breakthrough in marine biodiversity monitoring that could scale reef health assessment globally.
stories.source_quote: the frame is designed to position the array around a 360° camera (Insta 360, X3, Shenzhen, Guangdong, China) with an underwater housing
stories.source_type: peer-reviewed journal (Methods in Ecology and Evolution, September 2025)
stories.verification_note: Paper explicitly names Insta360 X3 in methods section. Source URL returned 403 to WebFetch (bot detection, not paywall — publicly accessible to humans). Quote sourced from search result snippets. Recommend human verify via full paper access.
stories.outreach_draft: Hi Marc, we came across your UPAC-360 paper in Methods in Ecology and Evolution — the combination of spatial audio and 360° video to identify reef fish species by sound is remarkable work. We noticed you used an Insta360 X3 as the camera component. We'd love to feature your coral reef bioacoustics research in our creator spotlight. Would you be open to a brief chat?

stories.name: Lukasz Mazur
stories.location: Chapel Hill, NC, USA (UNC School of Medicine / MaiaZura)
stories.story_summary: Surgical educator Lukasz Mazur and his team at UNC Chapel Hill developed MaiaZura, a VR surgical training platform that uses an Insta360 Titan camera in 11K resolution to capture third-person observer views of operating room procedures. Described in JMIR Medical Education (May 2025), the platform enables trainees to experience surgical cases from multiple perspectives in immersive VR. A UNC news article from January 2026 covered the platform's expanding use.
stories.why_it_matters: Demonstrates Insta360 Titan's role in medical education — capturing OR procedures in 11K 360° resolution for immersive VR surgical training at a major academic medical center.
stories.source_quote: a third-person observer view was recorded for each scene with the Insta360 Titan in 11K resolution
stories.verification_note: Quote confirmed via PMC12061349 search result snippets. Source URL returned 403 to WebFetch (bot detection). Note: database already contains 5 medical/surgical VR stories — human reviewer should assess whether to include for variety.

stories.name: Giovanna Calogiuri
stories.story_summary: Health researcher Giovanna Calogiuri at the University of South-Eastern Norway has used 360° video to study virtual nature as a therapeutic intervention. Her team filmed nature scenes with an Insta360 ONE X2 camera for a series of studies on how virtual nature exposure affects wellbeing, with findings published in JMIR Serious Games (2025). Her ongoing 360 Nature Hub project (2026) continues this research.
stories.why_it_matters: Academic validation of Insta360 for mental health and nature therapy research — an unusual application showing the camera's role in evidence-based wellbeing science.
stories.source_quote: The video-clips for their research were filmed using an Insta360 One X2 camera and subsequently edited in Adobe Premiere Pro 2022.
stories.verification_note: LOW CONFIDENCE: Insta360 ONE X2 attribution appears to originate from a 2023 technical report, not directly confirmed in the 2025 JMIR Serious Games paper. Camera model is also older (ONE X2 released 2020). Source URL returned 403 to WebFetch. Human reviewer should verify camera use in the 2025 paper specifically.
